chunks: And God wants to turn to you, but those who follow the desires want you to turn far astray.

key_terms.الشَّهَوَاتِ: desires or pleasures of the flesh
key_terms.يَتُوبَ: to turn in repentance or show mercy

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between God's will for us and the will of those who follow desires?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted through the lens of divine grace (tawassu') versus human agency, where Allah's will for repentance is universal, yet the 'great deviation' refers to those who actively choose to follow their lower selves (nafs al-ammara). The contrast highlights the spiritual danger of mistaking temporary worldly satisfaction for ultimate truth, a theme central to the concept of fitrah being obscured by desire.
